keyPoints: ["Richter magnitude is a base ten logarithm of intensity ratio","Subtract magnitudes to get the log of the intensity ratio","$10^{0.7}\\approx5$"]
modelAnswer:
Magnitude on the Richter scale is $M=\log\frac{I}{I_{0}}$, where $I$ is intensity.
Difference in magnitude $=8.5-7.8=0.7$, so
$\log\frac{I_{1920}}{I_{1923}}=0.7$, giving $\frac{I_{1920}}{I_{1923}}=10^{0.7}\approx5.01$.
The 1920 earthquake was about $5$ times stronger than the 1923 earthquake.
